questions.question: Which syntax is used to insert a user's first name into a Braze message?
questions.explanation: In Braze Liquid, personalization tags use double curly braces {{ }} with a dollar sign and curly brackets for standard attributes like {{ ${first_name} }}.

questions.question: What is the difference between {{ }} and {% %} in Braze Liquid syntax?
options: There is no difference; they are interchangeable
{{ }} outputs data and values; {% %} controls template rendering and logic
{{ }} is used for filters; {% %} is used for variables
questions.explanation: Double curly braces {{ }} are used for outputs (inserting values), while curly braces with percent signs {% %} are used for tags that control logic and template rendering.

questions.question: True or False: Filters can be used inside conditional statements (if/elsif) in Braze Liquid.
questions.explanation: Filters cannot be used directly in conditional statements. To use a filtered value in a conditional, assign it to a variable first using the assign tag.

questions.question: What does the 'capitalize' filter do in Braze Liquid?
options: Capitalizes the first letter of a string
Adds capital letters randomly throughout the text
questions.explanation: The capitalize filter converts the first letter of a string to uppercase and the rest to lowercase (e.g., 'hello world' becomes 'Hello world').

questions.question: True or False: Each conditional statement in Braze Liquid must have both an 'if' and 'endif' tag.
questions.explanation: Yes, every if statement must be closed with an endif tag. Without it, Braze will not render the message correctly or at all.

questions.question: Which operator should be used in Braze Liquid to check if two values are equal?
questions.explanation: The double equals operator (==) is used for comparison in Braze Liquid conditionals. A single equals (=) is used only for assigning variables.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'assign' tag in Braze Liquid?
options: To store a single value in a variable
To output data to the message
questions.explanation: The assign tag creates variables that store single values (booleans, numbers, strings). It can also apply a single filter in the same line.

questions.question: Which filter is used to convert a timestamp (like '2016-09-07 08:43:50 UTC') into a readable date format in Braze?
questions.explanation: The date filter converts timestamps into readable date formats. For example, {{ timestamp | date: '%B %d, %Y' }} converts it to 'September 07, 2016'.

questions.question: True or False: You can use the 'default' filter to provide a fallback value if a custom attribute is blank or null.
questions.explanation: Yes, the default filter provides a fallback value. For example, {{ ${first_name} | default: 'Valued Customer' }} displays 'Valued Customer' if first_name is blank.

questions.question: What syntax error occurs when you use triple curly braces {{{ }}} for Liquid personalization in Braze?
options: It is not valid Braze syntax and will fail
It converts the value to uppercase
questions.explanation: Triple braces {{{ }}} are not valid Braze Liquid syntax. The correct syntax uses double curly braces {{ }}. Triple braces are a common syntax error.

questions.question: Which tag is used to store multiple lines of text or complex expressions in Braze Liquid?
questions.explanation: The capture tag stores a block of text that may include multiple variables, strings, or complex expressions. It's preferred over assign for complex values like URLs.

questions.question: True or False: When using Braze Liquid, quote types matter—curly quotes ('') and straight quotes ('') are treated the same.
questions.explanation: Quote types matter significantly. Braze requires straight quotes ('') not curly quotes (''). Curly quotes (often from copy-pasting) cause Liquid errors.

questions.question: What does the 'size' filter do when applied to an array in Braze Liquid?
options: Returns the first element of the array
Returns the number of items in the array
Sorts the array in ascending order
Removes duplicate items from the array
questions.explanation: The size filter returns the count of items in an array. For example, {{ catalog_items | size }} outputs how many items a catalog selection returns.

questions.question: In Braze Liquid, which filter converts all text to uppercase?
questions.explanation: The upcase filter converts all characters in a string to uppercase. For example, {{ 'hello' | upcase }} outputs 'HELLO'.

questions.question: True or False: You can use Liquid filters in the for loop index in Braze.
questions.explanation: Filters cannot be used in for loops or array access brackets directly. To use a filtered value, assign it to a variable first.

questions.question: Which tag fetches a specific item from a Braze catalog in Liquid?
questions.explanation: The catalog_items tag is used to fetch items from a Braze catalog. For example, {% catalog_items Games 1234 %} fetches item 1234 from the Games catalog.

questions.question: True or False: In Braze Liquid, you must declare the catalog before referencing items in an if statement.
questions.explanation: Yes, you must declare the catalog and fetch items using the catalog_items tag before you can reference them in conditional statements.

questions.question: Which operator is used to check if a value does NOT equal something in Braze Liquid?
questions.explanation: The not-equal operator (!= ) is used in conditionals. For example, {% if status != 'active' %} checks if status is not equal to 'active'.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'default' filter when used with custom attributes in Braze?
options: To set the data type of the attribute
To provide a fallback value if the attribute is blank or null
To automatically format the attribute value
To encrypt the attribute for privacy
questions.explanation: The default filter provides a fallback message or value when a personalization attribute is missing, blank, or null.

questions.question: True or False: Liquid assignments or captures made in one message component (like subject line) are available in another component (like body).
questions.explanation: No, Braze renders each message component separately. Variables created in one field are not available in another. You must repeat the Liquid in each field.

questions.question: Which filter removes HTML tags from a string in Braze Liquid?
questions.explanation: The strip_html filter removes all HTML tags from a string, leaving only the text content.

questions.question: In Braze Liquid, what does the 'split' filter do?
options: Divides a string into an array using a specified separator
Removes a specified substring from text
Converts a string to an array of characters
questions.explanation: The split filter divides a string into an array based on a specified separator. For example, {{ 'hello,world' | split: ',' }} creates ['hello', 'world'].

questions.question: True or False: The 'case' and 'when' tags in Braze Liquid support arbitrary comparison operators like > and <.
questions.explanation: Case/when tags only support equality comparisons, not arbitrary operators. Each branch compares the case expression to a when value using equality (like ==).

questions.question: Which method should be used to avoid syntax errors when inserting catalog Liquid tags in Braze?
options: Type the tags manually in plain text
Use the + plus button in the message composer to insert tags automatically
Copy and paste from external code editors
questions.explanation: Braze recommends using the + plus button in the message composer to insert catalog Liquid tags automatically to avoid syntax errors.

questions.question: What does the 'unless' tag do in Braze Liquid?
options: It is the same as an 'if' statement
It evaluates a condition and executes code only if the condition is false
It skips a message if there's an error
questions.explanation: The unless tag is the opposite of if. It executes code only when the condition is false. For example, {% unless user_active %} displays content only for inactive users.

questions.question: True or False: In Braze Liquid, you can use parentheses to group complex boolean expressions like (a and b) or c.
questions.explanation: Braze Liquid doesn't support parentheses for grouping. To handle complex logic, use nested if statements or assign intermediate variables instead.

questions.question: Which filter adds a prefix or suffix to a string in Braze Liquid?
questions.explanation: The prepend filter adds text at the beginning, and the append filter adds text at the end. For example, {{ 'world' | append: '!' }} outputs 'world!'.

questions.question: True or False: The 'assign' tag can apply filters in the same line.
questions.explanation: Yes, the assign tag can apply a single filter in the same line. For example, {% assign name = first_name | capitalize %} assigns the capitalized first name to the variable.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct syntax for referencing a custom attribute in Braze Liquid? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: Custom attributes in Braze Liquid require the ${ } syntax within double curly braces. Option 1 is basic syntax, and option 2 shows using a filter with the default syntax.

questions.question: What is the best practice to avoid unwanted whitespace in Braze messages when using multi-line Liquid conditionals?
options: Add extra spaces between lines for readability
Write the conditional on a single line or use hyphens inside tag delimiters to strip whitespace
Use the 'remove_newlines' filter after all Liquid
Avoid using conditionals and use hardcoded text instead
questions.explanation: To avoid unwanted whitespace, write Liquid conditionals on a single line or use hyphens in tag delimiters like {%- if -%} to strip surrounding whitespace.
